QMJHL: Five takeaways from Cape Breton Eagles win over Moncton Wildcats, Oct. 4, 2026

'I thought out best players were our best players today'

Author of the article:
By Jeremy Fraser
Published Oct 04, 2026
Last updated Oct 05, 2026
7 minute read
Article content
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:40
Instaread

The Cape Breton Eagles (2-1-0-3) picked up their first win of the season on home ice on Sunday afternoon, defeating the Moncton Wildcats (5-1-0-0) 4-2 in front of 2,252 fans at Centre 200 in Sydney.

The loss was Moncton’s first of the season, snapping the New Brunswick-based club’s five-game winning streak to open the 2026-27 Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League regular season.

Cape Breton entered Sunday’s contest coming off a 4-3 shootout loss to the Saint John Sea Dogs on Friday night in Sydney.

Article content

FIVE TAKEAWAYS

Article content

FINDING CHEMISTRY

Article content

For the second consecutive game, the Cape Breton Eagles continued to progress with their team chemistry. With several new faces in the lineup compared to last season, it was known that chemistry would take time to develop.

Article content

Other than defenceman Will Murphy, it was the first time this season that the club had its full lineup with Maxim Schäfer being reassigned to the team from the Washington Capitals last week over the weekend.

Article content

It was clear early on in the game that the team was feeling more comfortable together, and it showed in the first period with the club going into the intermission with a 2-0 lead.

Article content
Advertisement 2
Story continues below
This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below.
Article content

The Eagles bent a little bit in the third period with Moncton taking the play to Cape Breton, but the Sydney-based club didn’t break and earned their first win of the season at home.

Article content

Article content

SCHAFER-SCHNEIDER-LEFEBVRE LINE

Article content

A line that first formed on Friday night against Saint John had a strong game on Sunday afternoon.

Article content

The line of Maxim Schäfer, Elias Schneider and Liam Lefebvre was dominant throughout the game, creating several scoring chances throughout the afternoon. Schäfer and Lefebvre spent time together while in Chicoutimi last season, while Schneider and Schäfer have played together on the German national junior team.

Article content

Schäfer, Lefebvre and Schneider connected for the Eagles’ second and third goals in the contest. Schäfer’s second period goal eventually held up as the game-winner.

Article content

If the three continue to play together and get more familiar with each other, it could be one of, if not the best, line in the QMJHL moving forward.

Article content

RIAN CHUDZINSKI

Article content

If there was one player on the Moncton Wildcats that stood out in the game, it would have to be Rian Chudzinski on Sunday.

Article content

The 18-year-old Anaheim Ducks prospect played well on the Wildcats’ top line with Liam Kilfoil and Noah Survilas.

Article content

He only recorded one assist in the contest, but he was very engaged in the game, drawing two penalties, while posting four shots on goal, two penalty minutes, five hits and a –2 rating.

Article content

He continued his point streak with the assist. The American now has two goals and five points in three games, dating back to last month.

Article content

Chudzinski will be a key player offensively for the Wildcats this season.

Article content

ROMAIN LITALIEN

Article content

The 18-year-old made his return to the Eagles’ lineup on Friday night after an injury last February forced him to miss the 2026 playoffs, and it didn’t take him long to get on the scoreboard.

Article content

Litalien opened the scoring in the game for Cape Breton on Sunday afternoon. It was his first goal since Jan. 30, 2026, against the Newfoundland Regiment in Sydney.

Article content

Litalien has been on the ice since August but didn’t play in any of the team’s pre-season games and missed the first four games of the regular season.

Article content
Advertisement 3
Story continues below
This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below.
Article content

It’s going to take time for him to shake off the rust and get used to the pace of the league again, but we’re talking about a guy who had 17 goals and 47 points in 52 games last season.

Article content

Now that he has his first goal of the season, you can bet there’s more to come.

Article content

Litalien also added an assist and finished the game with two points.

Article content

REGULATION WIN

Article content

It took six games, but the Eagles finally have their first victory in regulation time.

Article content

Prior to the game, Cape Breton’s only victory of the season came on Sept. 26 when they defeated the Saint John Sea Dogs 5-4 in overtime.

Article content

On home ice, the Eagles had dropped their first three games in a shootout. Cape Breton has eight straight shootout losses, dating back to last December.

Article content

Since the start of the season last month, Cape Breton has earned seven out of a possible 12 points in their first six games.

Article content

In a strong Eastern Conference, you can surely expect there to be a lot of three-point games this season.

Article content
Article content
Article content

COACH SAYS

Article content

“I thought out best players were our best players today, I mean, they were our best players on Friday, it was just one of those games on Friday night, but we continued to play the way we did, we left off right where we were today from Friday night and we were rewarded with good defensive play today.” – Cape Breton Eagles head coach Jason Clarke on his team’s overall play on Sunday.

Article content
Advertisement 4
Story continues below
This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below.
Article content

“It’s starting to come around. You have to also understand, I think our fan base and season-ticket holders have to understand that we had eight guys out of the lineup for the first month with guys in and out. We’re trying to put systems in and guys are playing different positions when they’re here, they’re on the power play, they’re off the power play, guys are playing their off positions and all of sudden we get two guys back and then guys have to move around again and then we get four or five guys back. It’s tough on the guys that were here, but the guys that were here all the way through the camp did a fantastic job for us. We only had one regulation loss coming into this game, so it’s not like we weren’t doing things well, it’s just we needed to polish up on a few things well. Two things that we talked about was defending and our reads and our breakouts. Friday night was our best breakout night of the year and I think today we were as close or as good.” – Cape Breton Eagles head coach Jason Clarke on his team’s chemistry

“Schafer and Lefebvre have played together before and Schneider is a very intelligent hockey player, his hockey IQ is off the chart, so it just made sense to put those guys together and they’ve had all kinds of offensive opportunities and they have size, they have speed and Schneider is probably one of the smartest players in this league, so to be able to play with two guys like that I’m sure he’s pretty happy as well.” – Cape Breton Eagles head coach Jason Clarke on the line of Liam Lefebvre, Maxim Schäfer and Elias Schneider.

EXTRA NOTES

Article content

Eagles firsts: Maxim Schäfer scored his first goal as an Eagle in the second period on Sunday afternoon. Meanwhile, Lucas Beckman won his first game at home in an Eagles uniform. Beckman picked up his first win of the season and first as an Eagle on Sept. 26 in Saint John, N.B.

Article content

Spencer Thornborough (MON): The Wildcats’ 10th-round pick in 2024 scored his first career QMJHL goal in the game. He tipped home a Noah Survilas shot to cut the Eagles’ lead to 3-2 in the third period.

Article content

Faceoff dominance: Cape Breton continued to perform well at the faceoff dot, winning 36 of 57 faceoffs in the contest.

Article content

Aiden McCullough (CAP): The third-year blueliner has stepped up on the physical side of the game in the last two contests. The 19-year-old had three hits in the contest on Sunday afternoon.

Article content

Three Stars

Article content

Article content
